compiled_state.title: [implementation-plan]: fitness-function-as-scaffolding approach missing first-baseline-capture step -> BASELINE_VIOLATIONS pattern not documented as standard
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## 1. Technical Environment
* **DSO version:** 1.16.11
* **Context:** /dso:implementation-plan fitness-function-as-scaffolding on Nava Ruby/Rails template

## 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior
When /dso:implementation-plan generates fitness-function-as-scaffolding for any spec (architectural, style, naming), it should document the BASELINE_VIOLATIONS pattern as the mandatory first step:

1. Run the fitness function against the existing codebase FIRST
2. Capture all current violations as BASELINE_VIOLATIONS (allowlist)
3. Write the spec to enforce 'no violations beyond baseline' (BASELINE_VIOLATIONS.any? { |f| subject.include?(f) } => skip for existing; enforce for new)
4. Ship a companion sanity spec verifying BASELINE_VIOLATIONS.size > 0 prevents silent empty-baseline bypass

This is the Rubocop --auto-gen-config idiom applied to architectural fitness functions. Any project using DSO on top of existing code (Nava templates, Rails new + DSO bolt-on) benefits. Without it, the generated spec fails immediately on day one.

#### Actual Behavior
The implementation-plan SKILL.md generates fitness-function specs without a baseline-capture step. The spec is written assuming a greenfield codebase. When run against existing code (e.g., cognito_adapter.rb and application_mailer.rb already reading ENV directly), the spec fails immediately on first run. The critical reviewer correctly identified this as a 'fitness-function-as-scaffolding' failure.

#### Impact
Every DSO onboarding onto an existing codebase (Nava templates, legacy repos) will hit this issue. The spec is useless on day one without the baseline, making the scaffolding approach a net negative compared to no spec at all.

## 3. Root Cause Hypothesis
/dso:implementation-plan SKILL.md fitness-function-as-scaffolding section does not include:
- Step 0: Run fitness function against existing codebase to discover baseline violations
- BASELINE_VIOLATIONS pattern for allowlisting existing offenders
- Companion sanity spec (spec on the spec) to prevent silent empty-baseline bypass

The BASELINE_VIOLATIONS + companion sanity spec pattern (analogous to Rubocop --auto-gen-config) should be a first-class concept in the DSO fitness-function guidance.
